properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/07/2025 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/07/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
Violation ID: 8228338
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/07/2025
Comments: On 04/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1045 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~310-332us/cm.There are 2 recently completed wells located onsite; the well permits are posted at the site entrance, however, I did not observe any tags on the wells (photo #2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which contained less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and is held in secondary containment (photo #5).Numerous temporary storage tanks are noted onsite for ongoing flow back activities, these tanks are held in secondary containment structures which retain sufficient storage capacity (photos #6 and 7). 6 upright brine storage tanks are also noted onsite but are not held in secondary containment (photo #8). 2 residual waste containers were also observed not held in secondary containment (photo #9).Perennial vegetative cover continues to grow in the areas surrounding the site (photo #10). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and is up to date (photo #11). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photos #12). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control and it appears to be functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Installing well tags on the wellheads. -Placing the upright brine storage tanks in secondary containment if they still contain a regulated substance to prevent violations from being cited against 25 PA 78a57(c).-Placing the residual waste containers in secondary containment.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Permit API: 083-50409
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/26/2021
Comments: This spill occurred sometime in the previous few months but was not reported to DEP. It was noted on a routine inspection by WQSS Rob Bechtel and myself en route to check another site. It appears as though a line leaked and allowed an unknown quantity of crude oil to be released to the site. Some volume flowed off the site and entered a spring run/UNT of Twomile Run. Crude oil was apparent in pools in several areas and fresher product was caught in moss lining the channel of the spring. It then appears to have flowed some 300 feet and entered another UNT of Twomile Run. The operator placed a boom in this stream at some point prior to the discovery of this spill by myself. Some sheen was apparent in leaf piles at this point, but no fresh product was noted. The operator was contacted and they were on the lease at the time. Immediate cleanup options were discussed, including installation of two siphon dams in the initial spring run and use of absorbent pads to catch any oil seeping from the banks. Further inspection will be performed as necessary. Violations are noted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/03/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 946420
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2022
Comments: On March 3, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline, Brooke Millisock, and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of 1,600 barrels of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. The southwest infiltration berm area of excavation has been uncovered and has filled with water. The water from the southwest infiltration berm area is overflowing the excavation depth and is flowing under a tarp. Due to the tarp covering the downgradient area of the excavation, the water overflowing could not be observed and could not be determined to be causing any erosion. The conductivity of the water in the in southwest excavation area was 104 uS/cm. The conductivity of the water in the southwest catch box of the well pad was 374 uS/cm. STL Resources continues to vacuum the water that has been collecting out of the catch boxes on the northwest and southwest corners of the well pad. The conductivity of the water in the northwest catch box was 7,800 uS/cm. Two seeps were observed near the northwest catch box, daylighting out of the slope of the well pad that had been previously excavated. The conductivity of the water in the seeps was 7,200 uS/cm. The water from the seeps is flowing in to an area that has been excavated and is covered by a tarp. The area under the tarp is a low spot in the excavation area the seep water appears to be contained in the low spot. Conductivity screening of the water in the remainder of the northwest infiltration berm excavation area resulted in conductivity less than 200 uS/cm. The DEP recommends collecting water from the seeps and delineating the area under the tarp for excavation of impacted soil. The DEP also recommends investigating where these seeps are originating from and installing corrective measures to eliminate the seeps. In addition to following up with the production fluid spill from January 8, 2022, the DEP did not observe any new erosion at the earthen infiltration berms noticed on February 28, 2022. The DEP did not observe any measures to correct the erosion that occurred. The DEP recommends adding temporary BMPs to these areas to help eliminate further erosion or to fix the earthen infiltration berms that had erosion issues. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

On 8/18/2020, I contacted operator representative Marc Strini to discuss the release. Comments: Follow-up site inspection on August 31, 2020 at ARD's COP Tract 231 well pad. Prior to my site inspection I spoke with Rick Hall of ARD via phone. The contractor discovered during excavation a small hole in the buried 2" steel line, which was the result of the undetermined amount of fluids released on August 28, 2020. According to Mr. Hall, approximately 50 tons of impacted gravel/soil were removed during excavation on August 28, 2020. Impacted gravel/soils were placed on secondary containment stationed onsite and the materials were covered. Impacted gravel/soils were observed during my inspection. Water was observed on the secondary containment with field screenings ranging from 52.8 uS/cm- 65.1 uS/cm. The Department recommends removing the rain water from the secondary containment.After excavation and repairing a section of the 2" dump line, the operator opted to leave the trench open and staked off with orange safety fence. According to Mr. Hall, there are three pipe lines running in the same ditch line. The first is the 2" steel dump line located at approximately 2' 8" deep below the surface. A 3" steel discharge line located in the same ditch line and a 6" steel suction line located approximately 4 feet away from the 2" dump line and is approximately 5' 8" below the surface. Mr. Hall stated that a bed of sand is located beneath the 6" suction line and conductivity readings were elevated in sections of that sand. Tuscarora Geological & Environmental Services collected samples from the impacted sand area. Mr. Hall requested that the sample results be expedited. Samples results are pending.While I was onsite I viewed the open trench. I screened throughout the 2" dump line side of the trench and readings ranged from 0.100 mS/cm to 0.300 mS/cm. I screened on the 6" suction line side of the trench and I was getting elevated readings >4.00 mS/cm in an approximate 2' diameter area. These elevated readings were adjacent to where the 2" dump line was repaired. As I moved away from that 2' diameter area, screenings dropped to 0.100 mS/cm to 0.400 mS/cm.No new violations have been cited. Outstanding violations remain.

Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8260680
Permit API: 003-22553
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Findlay Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/05/2026
Comments: On January 5 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/4/2026 (CTS 394386). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nate Smiell.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. The Department was unable to assess site stabilization due to snow coverage.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. According to Mr. Smiell, 8 of the wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, and 9H) are completed/active wells. These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2026
Comments: I conducted a site inspection on the morning of July 27, 2026 with the property owner. The inspection was concerning a brine release that was reported to the Department on July 25, 2026 by Jim Stiffler of Apollo Resources. According to Mr. Stiffler, the property owner was moving a trailer on the evening of July 24, 2026 and hit a 3" flange on the brine tank with the trailer, resulting in a brine release of 3,200 gallons of brine fluids.During the inspection I viewed the production equipment and the brine release area. Sandy, wet soils, and dead vegetation was observed in the brine release pathway. Approximately 6" of brine fluids still remain in the 100 BBL brine tank. Brine fluids traveled approximately 64' from the brine tank and approximately 30' wide. An old filled in pit from when the well was drilled is located in the pathway of the brine release. I screened multiple soil locations using a Hanna soil probe. Conductivity readings >4.00 mS/cm were observed.A stream (South Fork Beech Creek) is located downslope of the well site. I screened the stream both upstream and downstream of the brine release, readings were 48 uS/cm upstream and 52 uS/cm downstream.Due to the amount of brine fluid's released/reported, the Department recommends pursing Act 2 for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/16/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/16/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 959604
Permit API: 081-21884
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/16/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted due to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 15 gallons of hydraulic oil from a crane while it was traveling from the B pad to the A pad on the night of 6/15/22. I met with company man Walt Arnold on Pad B initially. He informed me that the access road had already been scraped the night before to remove the hydraulic oil from the access roads of Pads A and B. We then traveled to Pad A where he showed me the crane which was sitting on secondary containment. Next we each traveled back to the B Pad and along the way I stopped several times to inspect the access road. No hydraulic oil was observed on the access road. On pad B, I first inspected the area of the pad which had been impacted by the release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water on 6/9/22. More fluid was present on the pad surface, as well as on the secondary containment, than was present during the inspection the previous day. Mr. Arnold informed me that it had rained heavily overnight. The fluid in this area of the pad had an electrical conductivity (EC) below 800 uS/cm as measured in several spots. The EC in the sump in the stormwater channel was 742 uS/cm. The EC at the channel outlet at the corner of the pad was 865 uS/cm. Two other areas of the pad appeared to have elevated EC readings. Puddles on the pad surface near the upright produced water tanks closest to the freshwater tank had an EC of 1.8 mS/cm. More puddles on the pad surface near the secondary containment where the coiled tubing unit had been rigged up had an EC of 5.6 mS/cm. The fluid on the secondary containment here had an EC of 9.8 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was in the process of sucking up the fluid from this section of secondary containment. Violations noted for the hydraulic oil release and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/31/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8212369
Permit API: 083-51666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/31/2024
Comments: Upon being made aware of a crude oil release near this conventional well, I contacted Pennhills and learned that a steel gathering line located along the eastern side of the road (downslope of this well) was found to be compromised on December 9, 2024 and actions were taken to repair the line and remediate impacted media at that time. Since that time, Pennhills has decommissioned and vac'd out all fluid from the compromised line and are currently using a different gathering line that parallels the western edge of the road to carry fluids from this well and others located beyond this location. Representatives of Pennhills stated that the bulk of the earth disturbance along the eastern edge of the road was conducted to locate the portion of the line that was leaking and that they constructed an underflow dam downslope of the road to contain residual product that continues to leach from the road bank due to the abundance of larger rocks and roots in the area. Upon my arrival for this inspection, I observed the disturbed area along the eastern edge of the road that accesses this well. There was no visual evidence of crude oil across this disturbance, which was temporarily stabilized with seed and mulch. Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

Comments: Brian Shank and I met Ray Hepler at Farrington and Hepler Gas and Oil, Inc.'s Wheeler W12 well site (API 065-26269) in Washington Twp., Jefferson Co. Ray was onsite remediating the production fluid release first noted on Inspection Record No. 3765883. Soil conductivity readings near the production tank were greater than 1000 pS/cm. Ray stated he will remove this contaminated soil. Ray showed Brian and I a waste manifest for soil from Jefferson County. He stated this was soil disposed from the Wheeler well sites. We asked him to send the Department a copy of this manifest. The pipe stored onsite was loaded onto a trailer for removal. The outstanding violation associated with storing drilling supplies and equipment not needed for production on the well site without written consent of the surface landowner will be closed.After Ray completes the clean up of API 065-26269, please send the Department a report documenting the cause of the spill, the estimated amount of the spill, and the details of the clean up. Please include the soil conductivity reading collected throughout the remediation. Send the Department all waste manifests documenting proper disposal of contaminated soil from API 065-26269. After the Department receives, reviews and accepts the clean up report, the outstanding violations for API 065-26269 will be closed.

Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 874738
Permit API: 131-20033
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-01-22
Comments: At time of inspection, 23 degs. and sunny. There are (5) wells on this pad, with (1) open well slot. All (5) wells are in production, they are the N 1H, 2H, N 3H, S 4H and the 5H. All the wells have the (13x9) and the(9x5) annuli plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and are T'd into a 2" common line venting to the production tanks. All cellars are full water. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. (1/14/20) was used to check for gas at well heads, and during walk around pad. - A Follw Up Inspection (FUI) is being performed today on the 5H. CALLC. Well tender (Craig Shores) was on site to isolate the (9x13) annulus. After isolating the annulus and allowing it to vent for (10) minutes, a gas check was performed and no was was detected in the (9x13) annulus. During todays inspection no bubbling was noticed in cellar and no gas was detected w/ gas meter in ambient air. - Individual pressure readings taken from SCADA gauges. - 5H - prod. tree press.: 803.5psi., prod. csg. press.: 925.2 psi., (5x9) annulus press.: 9.4 psi., (9x13) annulus press.: 8.3 psi., prod. line press.:799.7 p - There is self contained ancillary equipment on the pad. - No other obvious concerns or violations noted.
